clean_methods: Context: Core measurement of sub- and suprathreshold CA1PC activity during novel exploration. Method: We will use voltage imaging to investigate the temporal dynamics of sub- and suprathreshold neuronal activities in CA1PCs during novel exploration.

Context: Genetic expression of a voltage indicator enabling simultaneous multi-cell sub- and suprathreshold measurements. Method: Our approach involves expressing the voltage indicator Voltron2 in CA1 pyramidal cells, which will allow us to measure both suprathreshold and subthreshold membrane potentials from multiple CA1PCs simultaneously.

Context: Head-fixed spatial exploration system for imaging during novel environment acquisition. Method: We will employ an air-lifted plastic track system that allows mice to explore an environment while remaining head-fixed under a microscope.

Context: Novelty control ensuring that imaging occurs during first exposure to the recording environment. Method: To ensure a genuinely novel experience, all pre-training and habituation will be performed in a separate room distinct from the recording setup. On imaging day, mice will be introduced to the recording room for the first time and initially confined to a specific corner of the track before being allowed to explore freely during imaging.

Context: Simultaneous behavioral and hippocampal network recording to link synchrony with behavior and oscillations. Method: We will simultaneously monitor animals' positions and speed within the track while recording local field potential (LFP) from the contralateral side of the hippocampus.

Context: High-speed, high-resolution voltage imaging acquisition for capturing spikes and subthreshold dynamics. Method: Fluorescence sensors will be excited using a 532-nm laser, and images will be acquired at 2kHz with high spatial resolution to capture both spiking activity and subthreshold membrane dynamics.

Context: Primary analysis of population synchrony, ensemble size, and statistical significance. Method: Detection and analysis of synchronous ensembles by counting spikes from all neurons within sliding windows and comparing to jittered controls. We will compare original data with jittered controls where spike timings are randomly perturbed while maintaining spike rates. We will quantify ensemble sizes, synchronization strength between cell pairs, and the temporal relationship between synchronous events and both theta oscillations and ripple events.

Context: Direct test of whether subthreshold membrane voltage dynamics underlie synchronous ensemble activity. Method: Examination of subthreshold membrane voltage dynamics in relation to synchronous events
Context: Population-level timing analysis of synchronous activity. Method: Calculation of grand average cross-correlograms (CCGs) to assess population synchrony timing
Context: Identification of network oscillations relevant to memory acquisition and consolidation. Method: Analysis of LFP traces to detect theta oscillations and ripple events

Context: Relationship between synchronous ensembles and network oscillations. Method: We will also investigate the relationship between synchronous ensembles and network oscillations by aligning LFP traces with detected synchronous events.

Context: Spatial memory analysis linking place-cell tuning to synchronous ensemble participation. Method: Assessment of spatial tuning properties to identify place cells and analyze their relationship to synchronous activity. Finally, we will examine the spatial coding properties of neurons participating in synchronous ensembles, particularly focusing on how synchronization strength relates to the similarity of place field tuning between neuron pairs.

Context: Behavioral modulation of synchronous ensembles. Method: We will analyze data across different behavioral states (locomotion vs. immobility) to determine how synchronous ensembles vary with animal behavior.
